questions.prompt: A right triangle has sides \(8\), \(15\), and \(17\). For an angle whose opposite side is \(8\), find \(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\), and \(\tan\theta\).
questions.answer:
The hypotenuse is \(17\), the opposite side is \(8\), and the adjacent side is \(15\). Therefore
\[
\sin\theta=\frac{8}{17},\qquad \cos\theta=\frac{15}{17},\qquad \tan\theta=\frac{8}{15}
\]

The angle \(5\pi/6\) is in quadrant II with reference angle \(\pi/6\). Thus sine is positive and cosine is negative:
\[
\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}=\frac12,\qquad \cos\frac{5\pi}{6}=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
\]
Therefore
\[
\tan\frac{5\pi}{6}=\frac{\sin(5\pi/6)}{\cos(5\pi/6)}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}=-\frac{\sqrt3}{3}
\]

questions.prompt: If \(\sin\theta=5/13\) and \(\theta\) lies in quadrant II, find \(\cos\theta\) and \(\tan\theta\).
questions.answer:
Use \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\):
\[
\cos^2\theta=1-\frac{25}{169}=\frac{144}{169}
\]
In quadrant II, cosine is negative, so
\[
\cos\theta=-\frac{12}{13}
\]
Then
\[
\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{5/13}{-12/13}=-\frac{5}{12}
\]

questions.prompt: A ramp makes an angle \(\theta\) with the horizontal and rises \(1.5\,\mathrm m\) over a horizontal distance of \(6.0\,\mathrm m\). Find \(\tan\theta\).
questions.answer:
Tangent is rise over run for this right triangle:
\[
\tan\theta=\frac{1.5}{6.0}=0.25
\]
